akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا﴾, that is: He revealed to it (أَوْحَى إِلَيْهَا).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ﴾: is moved for the coming of the Hour ﴿زِلْزَالَهَا﴾: its violent movement befitting its magnitude,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا﴾: its treasures and its dead, and casts them onto its surface,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ — the one who disbelieves in the Resurrection — ﴿مَا لَهَا﴾, in denial of that state.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: a badal (substitute) from «إذا», and its apodosis (jawāb) is: ﴿تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا﴾: it tells what was done on it, of good and evil,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿بِأَنَّ﴾: because ﴿رَبَّكَ أَوْحَى لَهَا﴾, that is, commanded it to do that. In the hadith: "It will testify against every male and female servant concerning everything done on its surface."

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ﴾: they depart from the place of reckoning ﴿أَشْتَاتًا﴾: scattered, one taking the right towards the Garden and one taking the left towards the Fire, ﴿لِيُرَوْا أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾, that is, their recompense, of the Garden or the Fire.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ﴾: the weight of a small ant ﴿خَيْرًا يَرَهُ﴾: will see its reward,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾: will see its recompense.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِذا زُلْزِلَتِ﴾: إذا is a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive, and a passive past verb; ﴿الْأَرْضُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿زِلْزالَها﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقالَها﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَقالَ الْإِنْسانُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لَها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb annexed to one like it, and it is a badal (substitute) for إذا; ﴿تُحَدِّثُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿أَخْبارَها﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the answer to إذا and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna and its noun; ﴿أَوْحى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿لَها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تحدث.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb annexed to one like it, and it is a badal (substitute) for the preceding one; ﴿يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿أَشْتاتاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿لِيُرَوْا﴾: a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason (taʿlīl), the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb يصدر.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿من﴾ is a conditional noun that puts the verb in the jussive, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَعْمَلْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to ذرة; ﴿خَيْراً﴾: tamyīz (specification); ﴿يَرَهُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the hāʾ is the direct object and the agent is latent; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position; the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ من, and the clause من… is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا﴾.
«الزِّلزال» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn Marwān narrated to me; he said: I said to al-Kalbī: What do you think of His word ﴿إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا﴾? He said: It is like His word ﴿وَيُخْرِجُكُم إِخْرَاجاً﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: The maṣdar was annexed to its owner, and in ordinary speech you would say: لأعطينَّك عطيتك (I shall surely give you your gift) when you mean [simply] a gift; but what brought it close to being permissible is its matching the verse-endings that come after it.
«الزِّلزال» with kasra is the maṣdar, and «الزَّلزال» with fatḥa is the noun. Likewise «القَعْقاع», the one who makes a clattering, is the noun, and «القِعقاع» is the maṣdar. And «الوَسواس» is Satan, and whatever whispers to you or speaks to you [inwardly]; it is a noun, while «الوِسواس» is the maṣdar.

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا﴾.
It casts out what is in it, of gold or silver or the dead.

farraa:3-4.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلإِنسَانُ مَا لَهَا﴾.
By «الإنسان» here He means the unbeliever. Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا﴾.
It will report what was done [146/a] upon it, good or evil.

farraa:5-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا﴾.
He says: it relates its news by the revelation of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, and by His permission to it. Then He said: ﴿لِّيُرَوْاْ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾; this — according to what the tafsīr has brought — is postponed [in meaning], and this [i.e. after «أوحى لها»] is its place; ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ ٱلنَّاسُ أَشْتَاتاً﴾ intervenes parenthetically between them, put forward while its meaning is postponed. The readers agreed on (لِيُرَوْا) [in the passive]; had it been read (ليَرَوا) [in the active], it would have been correct.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd], in place of (تحدّث) there is (تُنَبِّىءْ), and it is written (تنبّأ) with an alif.
﴿يَرَهُ﴾: you give the hāʾ sukūn (jazm), or you give it ḍamma (rafʿ).

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis {تُحَدِّثُ}; «زلزالها»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «لها»: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «يومئذ»: an adverb, badal (substitute) of {إِذَا}; the clause «تحدِّث» is the apodosis (jawāb) of {إِذَا}; «إذ»: an adverbial noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the tanwīn is a compensation for an omitted clause, i.e.: the day when the earth is shaken.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: (بأن ربك أوحى لها) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {تُحَدِّثُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «يومئذ»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يصدر»; «أشتاتًا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الناس»; «أعمالهم»: second object; and the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليروا» is attached to «يصدر».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «فمن يعمل» is conjoined to the preceding clause {يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ}; «خيرًا»: tamyīz (specification); and the clause «يره» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, Exalted is He (إذا زلزلت): (إذا) is an adverb of future time, and the governing word (ʿāmil) in it is (زلزلت). That is permissible because it has the meaning of a condition; what follows it is, in the implied structure, made jussive by it. So just as its governing what follows it is permissible, while in its status it is annexed (muḍāfa) to the clause after it, so too is it permissible for what follows it to govern it — just as with (من) and (ما) that are for the condition: what follows them governs them, and they [in turn] govern what follows them. [Translator's note: the printed text has a stray letter «ة» before «تعملان»; it has been left untranslated.] You say «من تكرم أكرمه» (whomever you honour, I will honour him) and «ما تفعل أفعل» (whatever you do, I will do): (ما) and (من) are in the position of the accusative by the jussive verb after them, while they themselves have made what follows them jussive. So (إذا), since it carries the meaning of the condition, has been treated like (ما) and (من), even though in the implied structure it is annexed to the clause after it.
His saying (زلزالها): a maṣdar (verbal noun), as you say «ضربتك ضربك» (I struck you your [manner of] striking). Its annexation to the pronoun is good so that the verse-endings agree on a single form. (الزلزال) with fatḥa is the noun, and with kasra it is the maṣdar; and it was said: both of them are maṣdars. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «وزلزلوا زلزالا» with fatḥa, and he read (زلزالها) with fatḥa.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (ما لها): (ما) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is interrogative, a complete noun (ism tāmm), and (لها) is the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His saying (فمن يعمل مثقال): (من) is conditional; it is a complete noun (ism tāmm) and a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (يره) is the khabar (predicate). The second one is like it.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تحدث﴾, which is the answer. And it was said: «إذا» is purely adverbial and what governs it is omitted, i.e. "they will be gathered" (يُحشرون). And it was said: «إذا» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the implied sense being: "remember when it is shaken" (اذكر إذا زلزلت).
﴿زلزلت﴾: a past verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the tāʾ is a particle of the feminine.
﴿الأرض﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿زلزالها﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿زلزلت﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it, and the clause ﴿إذا زلزلت﴾ is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وأخرجت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «أخرجت» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the tāʾ is a particle of the feminine.
﴿الأرض﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿أثقالها﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿أخرجت﴾ is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause ﴿زلزلت﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وقال﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «قال» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الإنسان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لها﴾: the lām is a preposition, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ما﴾; the clause ﴿ما لها﴾ is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause ﴿قال الإنسان﴾ is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause ﴿زلزلت﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تحدث﴾, and it is a badal (substitute) for ﴿إذا﴾ in the saying of the Exalted ﴿إذا زلزلت﴾, if «إذا» is taken to contain the sense of condition, and what governs it is what governs the replaced word; «يوم» is muḍāf, and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, implied because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied wording being: "on the day when the earth is shaken with its shaking, and the earth brings forth its burdens, and man says: what is with it?" (يوم إذ تزلزل الأرض زلزالها وتخرج الأرض أثقالها ويقول الإنسان ما لها).
﴿تحدث﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هي), referring back to the earth; the first object of «تحدث» is omitted, i.e. "it will tell people its news" (تحدث الناسَ أخبارَها).
﴿أخبارها﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿تحدث﴾, accusative by the fatḥa, and it is muḍāf, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿تحدث﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition, on the view that ﴿إذا﴾ is conditional; or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position, if ﴿إذا﴾ does not contain the sense of condition.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿بأن﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «أن» is an abrogating particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿ربك﴾: the noun (ism) of «أن», accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; «رب» is muḍāf, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أوحى﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو).
﴿لها﴾: the lām is a preposition, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أوحى﴾; the clause ﴿أوحى﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «أن», the clause ﴿أن ربك...﴾ is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ before it, and the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿بأن ربك...﴾ are attached to ﴿تحدث﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يصدر﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf, and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, implied because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿يصدر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿الناس﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿أشتاتا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الناس», accusative by the fatḥa.
﴿ليروا﴾: the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and «يروا» is an imperfect verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), accusative by an «أن» concealed after the lām, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the interpreted maṣdar from «أن» and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يصدر﴾; the clause ﴿يروا﴾ has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the concealed particle relative ﴿أن﴾, and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يروا﴾ is genitive by the lām of causation, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يصدر﴾.
﴿أعمالهم﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the fatḥa; the clause ﴿يومئذ يصدر الناس...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿فمن﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and «من» is a jussive-governing conditional noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يعمل﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the sukūn, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿مثقال﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, and it is muḍāf.
﴿ذرة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿خيرا﴾: tamyīz (specification) or a badal (substitute) for ﴿مثقال﴾, accusative by the fatḥa.
﴿يره﴾: an imperfect verb, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause of the condition and its answer is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿من﴾, and the clause ﴿من يعمل...﴾ is conjoined to the one before it, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ومن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «مَن» is a jussive-governing conditional noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يعمل﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the sukūn, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿مثقال﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, and it is muḍāf.
﴿ذرة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿شرا﴾: tamyīz (specification) or a badal (substitute) for «مثقال», accusative by the fatḥa.
﴿يره﴾: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the protasis and its answer are in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿من﴾, and the clause ﴿من يعمل...﴾ is conjoined to the one before it, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: إِذا is in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), and the operator in it is زلزلت. زِلْزالَها is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as one says أكرمتك كرامتك, the meaning being "an honouring"; likewise the meaning is "it was shaken with a shaking". The annexation (iḍāfa) was good so that the verse-endings would agree. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ hold that الزِّلزال (with kasra) is the maṣdar and الزَّلزال (with fatḥa) is a noun, and that one says waswasa waswāsan (with kasra), while al-waswās (with fatḥa) is the noun. ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read وَزُلْزِلُوا زِلْزالًا شَدِيداً [al-Aḥzāb: 11] with fatḥa, and read إِذا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزالَها [Translator's note: the printed vowelling is the standard one; al-Jaḥdarī's reading is presumably with fatḥa here too, زَلْزالَها].

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: (أثقال is) the plural of thiql; and al-thiql (heaviness) is in the ear [Translator's note: so in the text; the vowelling distinguishing the two words is not shown].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: ما is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a complete noun.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: (it is so) because the meaning of tuḥaddithu (relates) and tukhbiru (informs) is one. This indicates that the meaning of ḥaddathanā and akhbaranā is one.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: One also says waḥā lahu and ilayhi, in both (forms, with lām and with ilā).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ أَشْتاتاً: (أشتاتا is) accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ said: the readers agreed on لِيُرَوْا أَعْمالَهُمْ. Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Ḥātim reported that ʿAbbād ibn Kathīr said: it has reached me that the Prophet ﷺ read لِيُرَوْا أَعْمالَهُمْ [Translator's note: the printed vowelling is identical in both places; the reading attributed to the Prophet ﷺ here is لِيَرَوْا, active]. Abū Jaʿfar said: there is fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) in the speech according to the grammarians, i.e., "on that day it will relate its news, so that they may be shown their deeds".

nahhas-irab:7-8.t:
فَمَنْ is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a complete noun. يعمل is jussive (majzūm) by the condition. خَيْراً is accusative as specification (bayān) or as a badal (substitute) for مثقال. «يره» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the alif was dropped from it for the jussive. And likewise وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ (8).
The apparent sense of the speech indicates that everyone who does anything will see it, believer and disbeliever alike, and that the disbeliever is recompensed for his good deeds in this world by the warding off of harm; and likewise the ḥadīths are on this: that the disbeliever is recompensed for his good deeds in this world and will have no good in the Hereafter, and that the believer is the opposite of that: his portion is afflictions in this world, and his reward is kept in full for him in the Hereafter.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ}: «إذا» is conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb) is «تُحَدِّثُ», which is what makes it accusative according to the majority. Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted that its governor be «يَصْدُرُ». Others make its governor what comes after it and immediately follows it, even though that is governed by it through annexation in the implied structure; Makkī chose this, and he made it parallel to «مَنْ» and «ما», meaning that these two govern what follows them in the jussive, while what follows them governs them in the accusative; had he illustrated it with «أيّ», it would have been clearer. It was also said: its governor is implied, i.e. "they will be gathered". It was also said: "remember"; and in that case it leaves [the function of] adverb and condition.
His saying: {زِلْزَالَهَا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its fāʿil (agent). The meaning is: its quaking that it deserves and that its mass and magnitude require. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Similar to it is: "أكرِمِ التقيَّ إكرامَه، وأَهِنِ الفاسِقَ إهانتَه" (honour the God-fearing with the honour due to him, and humiliate the sinner with the humiliation due to him); or [it means] its quaking in full.» The majority read it with kasra on the zāy.
Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā [read it] with fatḥa. It was said: they are two maṣdars with one meaning. It was also said: the kasra form is a maṣdar and the fatḥa form is a noun. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Among the patterns there is no فَعْلال with fatḥa except in reduplicated [roots].» I say: some have made the fatḥa form in the sense of an active participle, like صَلْصَال in the sense of مُصَلْصِل, and that has been discussed already. His saying: «Among the patterns there is no فَعْلال» means: as a rule; otherwise «ناقةٌ خَزْعال» (a limping she-camel) has occurred.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {مَا لَهَا}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). This refutes the saying of whoever said that the ḥāl (circumstantial) in such as {فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التذكرة مُعْرِضِينَ} [al-Muddaththir: 49] is obligatory lest the speech become uninformative, for there is no ḥāl here.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}, i.e. on the day when it is shaken. The governor of «يومئذٍ» is «تُحَدِّثُ» if you make «إذا» accusative by what follows it or by something omitted; and if you make its governor «تُحَدِّثُ», «يومئذٍ» is a badal (substitute) from it, and its governor is [either] the governor of [«إذا»], or something else because it [the badal] is on the intention of repeating the governor — a well-known disagreement.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تُحَدِّثُ», i.e. it narrates. It may also be attached to «أخبارَها» itself. It was also said: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and «أنَّ» with what is in its domain is a badal (substitute) from «أخبارَها». It was also said: the bāʾ is causal, i.e. because of Allah the Exalted's revealing to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: where are the two objects of "تُحَدِّثُ"? I say: the first of them is omitted, and the second is "أخبارَها"; its origin is: it narrates to creation its news; except that what is intended is to mention its narrating the news, not to mention creation, in order to magnify the Day. If you say: to what is the bāʾ attached in His saying "بأنَّ ربَّك"? I say: to "تُحَدِّثُ", because its meaning is: it narrates its news because of your Lord's revealing. The meaning may also be: it narrates your Lord [sic] by narrating that your Lord revealed to it its news, on the basis that its narrating that your Lord revealed to it is a narrating of its news, just as you say: "you gave me every advice by advising me in religion".» [Translator's note: «تُحَدِّثُ ربَّك» is as written; the sense requires something like "it narrates by narrating that your Lord revealed…", and «ربَّك» here may be a copying error.] The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «It is speech containing rubbish from which the Qurʾān is to be kept free.» I say: what rubbish is there in it, given its correctness and eloquence? But since its implied structure was long on account of conveying this fine meaning, he made it rubbish — far be it from that!
Then al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is possible that "بأنَّ ربَّك" is a badal from "أخبارَها", as though it were said: on that Day it will narrate its news, that your Lord revealed to it; because you say: حَدَّثْتُه كذا and حَدَّثْتُه بكذا (I told him such-and-such / of such-and-such).» The Shaykh said: «If the verb is sometimes made transitive by a preposition and sometimes transitive by itself, and the preposition is not redundant, then in its follower only agreement in case is permissible. So "استغفَرْتُ الذنبَ العظيمِ" with "الذنبَ" in the accusative and "العظيم" in the genitive is not permissible on the grounds that you may say "من الذنب"; nor "اخْتَرْتُ زيداً الرجالَ الكرامِ" with "الرجالَ" in the accusative and "الكرام" in the genitive; likewise you may not say "استغفرتُ من الذنبِ العظيمَ" with "العظيمَ" in the accusative, and likewise with "اخْتَرْتُ". If the preposition were redundant, following the position of the noun would be permissible, under its conditions as set out in the science of grammar; you say: "ما رأيتُ مِنْ رجلٍ عاقلاً", because "مِنْ" is redundant, and "مِنْ رجل عاقلٍ" following the wording; but it is not permissible to put "رجل" in the accusative and "عاقل" in the genitive on the grounds that the entry of "مِنْ" may be taken into account. If anything of that kind occurs, its domain is poetry.» End of quotation. I do not know how he makes al-Zamakhsharī liable for what he made him liable for, from all the questions he mentioned. For al-Zamakhsharī says: this is a badal from what precedes it; then he mentioned what justifies the entry of the bāʾ on the badal, namely that the bāʾ may enter on the substituted-for word, so that were the badal to take the place of the substituted-for word with the bāʾ, it would be permissible, because the governor is made transitive by it; and he mentioned what justifies the substituted-for word's being free of the bāʾ, saying: «because you say: حَدَّثْتُه كذا and حَدَّثْتُه بكذا». As for its being prohibited to say «استغفَرتُ الذنبَ العظيمِ» with «الذنبَ» in the accusative and «العظيمِ» in the genitive, to the end — there is nothing of that at all in al-Zamakhsharī's words.
The parallel of what al-Zamakhsharī said in the case of «استغفر» is that you say: «استغفرْتُ اللَّهَ ذنباً مِنْ شَتْمي زيداً» (I asked Allah's forgiveness for a sin — for my reviling Zayd); your saying «مِنْ شَتْمي» is a badal from «الذنب», and this is permissible without doubt.
His saying: {أوحى لَهَا}: There are several views on this lām. The first: it is in the sense of «إلى»; it was preferred to «إلى» only to accord with the verse-endings (fawāṣil). Al-ʿAjjāj said, describing the earth:
4614 - أَوْحَى لها القرارَ فاستقرَّتِ ... وشَدَّها بالرَّاسياتِ الثُّبَّتِ
(He inspired it to be still, so it became still, and fastened it with the firm-set mountains.)
The second: it keeps its basic sense, and «أوحى» is made transitive sometimes with the lām and sometimes with «إلى»; from it is the preceding verse. The third: the lām has its proper sense of cause, and the one to whom revelation is made is omitted, namely the angels; its implied form is: He revealed to the angels for the sake of the earth, i.e. for the sake of what they will do in it.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: either a badal (substitute) from the «يومئذٍ» before it, or accusative by «يَصْدُرُ», or accusative by an implied «اذْكُرْ» (remember).
His saying: {أَشْتَاتاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الناس»; it is the plural of شَتّ, i.e. dispersed [in groups] in safety and fear, in whiteness and blackness.
His saying: {لِّيُرَوْاْ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَصْدُرُ»; it was also said: to «أوحى», with what is between them parenthetical. The majority read it as passive; it is from seeing with the eye, so it is made transitive by the hamza to a second [object], namely «أعمالَهم». Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Qatāda and Ḥammāda [sic] ibn Salama — and it is related from Nāfiʿ; al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is the reading of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ» — read it as active; and the meaning is: [to see] the recompense of their deeds. [Translator's note: the name is written «حمادة»; the well-known reader is Ḥammād ibn Salama.]

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {خَيْراً}, {شَرّاً}: There are two views on their accusative. The more apparent of the two: they are a tamyīz (specification) of «مثقال», since it is a measure. The second: they are two badals (substitutes) from «مثقالَ».
His saying: {يَرَهُ}: the apodosis (jawāb) of the condition in both places. Hishām read the hāʾ of «يَرَهْ» with sukūn in continuous recitation in both words, and the rest of the Seven with ḍamma, joined to a wāw in continuous recitation and quiescent in pause, like all the pronominal hāʾs. This is what I read with. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] transmitted from Hishām and Abū Bakr its sukūn, from Abū ʿAmr its ḍamma with full lengthening, and from the rest of the Seven full lengthening in the first and sukūn in the second. End of quotation. That was mostly due to the pause at the end of the sūra; had they joined its end to the beginning of «al-ʿĀdiyāt», the rule would be full lengthening. This is what their principles require, as I stated earlier, and it is what is transmitted.
The majority read «يَرَهُ» as active. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Ḥaywa, and ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī in one transmission read «يُرَه» as passive. ʿIkrima [read] «يَراه» with the alif: either on the supposition of the jussive by omission of the implied vowel, or on the illusion that «مَنْ» is relative; the verification of this is mentioned near the end of [Sūrat] Yūsuf. Al-Zamakhsharī related that a Bedouin put «خيراً يَرَهُ» later [i.e. read the two verses in reverse order]; it was said to him: "You have put first and put last [what should not be]", and he recited:
4615 - خذا بَطْنَ هرشى أوقَفاها فإنَّه ... كِلا جانِبَيْ هرشى لَهُنَّ طريقُ
(Take the inner side of Harshā or its back, for both sides of Harshā are a road for them.)
End of quotation. He means that putting first and last are the same. This is not permissible at all, for it is an error that is not to be held as a reading.
الذَّرَّة — it was said: the small ant; and the smallest it is when a year has passed over it. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4616 - من القاصراتِ الطَرْفِ لو دَبَّ مُحْوِلٌ ... من الذَّرِّ فوق الإِتْبِ منها لأَثَّرا
(Of those who restrain their glances: were a year-old ant to creep over her shift, it would leave a mark.)

ukberi-tibyan:1-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا (١) وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا (٢) وَقَالَ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا لَهَا (٣) يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ): the governor (ʿāmil) of «إِذَا» is its apodosis (jawāb), namely the words of the Exalted «تُحَدِّثُ», or «يَصْدُرُ». (يَوْمَئِذٍ) is a badal (substitute) for «إِذَا». It is also said that the implied form is: «اذْكُرْ إِذَا زُلْزِلَتْ» (remember when [the earth] is shaken); on this view «تُحَدِّثُ» may govern «يَوْمَئِذٍ», or «يَوْمَئِذٍ» may be a badal.
«الزِّلْزَال» with a kasra is the maṣdar (verbal noun), and with a fatḥa it is the noun.

ukberi-tibyan:5-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَى لَهَا (٥) يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ النَّاسُ أَشْتَاتًا لِيُرَوْا أَعْمَالَهُمْ (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ): the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تُحَدِّثُ), [i.e.] the earth reports by what He revealed to it.
It is also said that it is redundant (zāʾida), and that «أَنَّ» [with its clause] is a badal (substitute) for (أَخْبَارَهَا).
(لَهَا) is in the sense of «إِلَيْهَا» (to it). It is also said that «أَوْحَى» is made transitive sometimes with lām and at other times with «عَلَى».
The second (يَوْمَئِذٍ) is a badal, or on the construal of «اذْكُرْ» (remember), or an adverbial (ẓarf) for «يَصْدُرُ».
(أَشْتَاتًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); its singular is «شَتّ». The lām in (لِيُرَوْا) is attached to «يَصْدُرُ».
It is read with the agent named (active) and with the agent left unnamed (passive), and it is from seeing with the eye, i.e. that they may be shown the recompense of their deeds.

ukberi-tibyan:7-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ (٧) وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ (٨)).
The words of the Exalted (خَيْرًا) and (شَرًّا): they are two badals (substitutes) for «مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ», and they may also be a tamyīz (specification). And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Zalzala
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إذا زُلْزِلَتِ الأرْضُ زِلْزالَها﴾ ("when the earth is shaken with its shaking"): when it is moved with a violent movement. The reading is ﴿زِلْزالَها﴾ with kasra on the zāy; and ”زَلْزالَها“ is permissible in speech, and it was read ”زَلْزالَها“. There is no pattern ”فَعْلالٌ“ with fatḥa on the fāʾ in the language except in reduplicated [roots], like ”اَلزِّلْزالُ“ and ”اَلصَّلْصالُ“. The preferred [reading] is kasra on the zāy, and fatḥa is permissible.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَأخْرَجَتِ الأرْضُ أثْقالَها﴾ ("and the earth brings out its burdens"): it brings out its treasures and its dead.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَقالَ الإنْسانُ ما لَها﴾ ("and the human being says: what is with it?"): this is the saying of the unbeliever, because he did not believe in the Resurrection, so he said: "What is with it?!", that is: for what reason is its shaking?!

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أخْبارَها﴾ ("on that Day it will relate its news"): ”يَوْمَئِذٍ“ is accusative (manṣūb) by His saying [i.e. the sense is]: "when it is shaken and brings out [its burdens] on that day". And the meaning of ﴿تُحَدِّثُ أخْبارَها﴾ is: it informs him of what was done upon it.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ النّاسُ أشْتاتًا لِيُرَوْا أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ ("on that Day people will come forth in scattered groups to be shown their deeds"): that is, they come forth separately: among them are those who did good and among them those who did evil.
And the reading is ﴿لِيُرَوْا أعْمالَهُمْ﴾; it is also related as ”لِيَرَوْا أعْمالَهُمْ“ ("that they may see their deeds"), but I know of no one who read it so. It is not permissible to read with what is permissible in Arabic if those from whom the reading has been taken did not read it so.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And the meaning of ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ﴾ ("so whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it"): its interpretation is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has counted the deeds of His servants, of good [and evil], and each will see his deed; then whomever Allah wishes to forgive, He forgives, and whomever He wishes to requite, He requites. And it was said: whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it in this world, and likewise "evil": he will see it in this world. And Allah knows best.
